# {{< var wip >}} Command Line Interface

`flower` is called from the command line with the following signature:

`flower COMMAND [ARGS] [OPTIONS]`

## Commands

A description of the available commands and their arguments and options
follow.

## {{< var wip >}} `view [ARGS]`

View the Data Package's metadata in the terminal.

#### Arguments

{{< var wip >}} `path` or `url`
: The local path or remote url to a Data Package. Defaults to `datapackage.json` (in the current directory).

#### Examples

```sh
flower view https:/...
```

Views the metadata for a Data Package located online in the terminal

### {{< var wip >}} `build [ARGS] [OPTIONS]`

Build documentation pages from the Data Package's metadata.

#### Arguments

{{< var wip >}} `path` or `url`
: The local path or remote url to a Data Package. Defaults to
`datapackage.json` (in the current directory).

#### Options

{{< var wip >}} `-s/--style TEXT`
: The style of the output document. One of `quarto-book`,
`quarto-resource-listings`, `quarto-resource-tables`, or `custom`. If
set to `custom`, the `--content` flag must be used to specify the custom
style. Defaults to `quarto-book`.

{{< var wip >}} `-c/--content LIST of TEXT or LIST of LISTS`
: A list of which content to include when the style is set to custom.
The following options are available `package`, `contributors`,
`licenses`, `sources`, `resources`, `resource-schema`,
`resource-licenses`, `resource-sources`, `resource-schema-fields`. This
can also be a list of lists, splitting the content into multiple pages
,e.g. `-c [[package], [sources]]` creates two pages, one with the
`package` metadata and one with the `sources` metadata.

{{< var wip >}} `-t/--template PATH or LIST of PATHS`
: Path to jinja template to use for custom output formats and styles,
e.g. custom formatting of an HTML page. To just change the extension of
the output files but keep the default formatting, and empty file can be
specified. Can also be a list of paths, one per page specified in
`--content`.

{{< var wip >}} `-o/--output PATH`
: The location to write the file. Can also be a list of locations, one
per page specified in `--content`. Defaults to `docs/`.

{{< var wip >}} `-i/--ci-template TEXT`
: Whether to include template files for continuous deployment with
a certain framework on GitHub. Currently the only option is `quarto`.
Defaults to not include the CI template files.

#### Examples

```sh
flower build
```

Builds a documentation site in qmd format for the data package in the
current working directory.

---

```sh
flower build my-folder/datapackage.json -s quarto-resource-listings -i quarto
```

Builds a documentation site in qmd format for the data package in
`my-folder`. The chosen style splits the documentation into several
pages. Template files are included for setting up continuous integration
with quarto on github.

---

```sh
flower build\
    -s custom\
    -c [[package], [contributors, licenses]]\
    -t [1st-page.html, 2nd-page.html]
```

Builds a documentation site in html format for the data package in the
current working directory. The custom style of the documentation creates
one page with the package metadata and a second page with info on the
contributors and license. Both pages are created using a custom HTML
template. (`\` is used to split the command on multiple lines.)
